items.title: Baby boy found alive in US after believed buried for 24 hours, police say
items.summary: SOUTH CAROLINA: An 11-month-old boy was found alive in South Carolina on Tuesday after he was believed to have been buried for about 24 hours, the Lexington County Sheriff's Department said. Just a few moments ago, we found little Koah, 11 months old, buried alive, clinging to life, crying — the most joyful sound you ever heard of a crying baby," Lexington County Sheriff Jay Koon said during a news conference. Koon said the infant's father, Michael Comer, was arrested on Monday night on burglary and resisting arrest.

items.title: MetMalaysia issues strong winds, rough seas warning
items.summary: Meanwhile, MetMalaysia issued a third-category warning for northeasterly winds exceeding 60kmph and waves higher than 4.5m in Northeastern Condore and Northwestern Reef North until tomorrow. A second-category warning was issued for Condore and parts of Reef North, while a first-category warning covers Palawan, Southeastern Reef North, Labuan, Layang-Layang, Samui and northern Tioman. A separate thunderstorm warning was also issued for several shipping areas, including the Straits of Melaka, Phuket, Samui, Tioman, Reef South, Condor, Bunguran, Sulu, Reef North, Palawan, Sulawesi, Layang-Layang and Labuan until 1pm today.

items.title: Nine people seriously hurt in South Korea bus crash involving multiple vehicles
items.summary: SEOUL: A bus crashed into multiple vehicles in the Bundang district of South Korea on Wednesday, leaving nine people seriously injured and 48 with minor injuries, according to the fire agency. The bus struck the vehicles at around 7.34am (2234 GMT on Tuesday), including some waiting at a traffic light, before crashing into a median barrier, the National Fire Agency said, citing a witness. The accident in Bundang, in Seongnam city south of Seoul, involved 32 vehicles, including four buses, a truck and 27 passenger cars, according to the agency.

items.title: High inventories weigh on CPO, but 2027 outlook brightens
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's record-high palm oil inventories could continue weighing on the commodity's near-term outlook, although analysts expect tightening supplies, weather-related production risks and stronger biodiesel demand to support crude palm oil (CPO) prices heading into 2027. Palm oil inventories climbed for the seventh consecutive month to 3.62 million tonnes in October, up 3.2 per cent month-on-month, as higher opening stocks and increased production outweighed stronger exports. PublicInvest, however, expects inventories to begin easing from November as oil palm trees enter their seasonal low-production period.

items.title: Loke makes final appearance with Transport Ministry staff
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Former Transport Minister Anthony Loke attended the Transport Ministry's (MOT) monthly assembly for the last time today, following his resignation which took effect last night. The Seremban MP's resignation took effect as soon as former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak arrived at his residence to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest. He was welcomed by Deputy Transport Minister Datuk Hasbi Habibollah and MOT secretary-general Datuk Seri Jana Santhiran Muniayan.

items.title: Malaysia's industrial growth resilient despite AI headwinds: economists
items.summary: They said the latest industrial production data reflected improving momentum, with the industrial production index (IPI) expanding 6.3 per cent year-on-year (YoY) in September, up from five per cent in August. On the September IPI performance, manufacturing output grew 9.4 per cent, accelerating from 7.4 per cent in August, while electricity production expanded 10.7 per cent against nine per cent previously. The manufacturing sector's stronger performance was broad-based, with export-orientated industries growing 10.6 per cent, compared with 9.9 per cent in August, while domestic-orientated manufacturing accelerated to seven per cent from 2.3 per cent.

items.title: SKA Capital soars 18.6pct in ACE Market debut
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: SKA Capital Bhd made a strong debut on the ACE Market on Wednesday, with its share price surging 18.6 per cent above its initial public offering (IPO) price, signalling strong investor appetite for the electrical engineering firm. The counter opened at 51 sen, eight sen or 18.6 per cent higher than its IPO price of 43 sen per share, before extending its gains to hit an intraday high of 57.5 sen. More to come © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: ‘Whether or not we accept it, we can vote’: Loke tells Melaka to use ballot box to convey feelings on Najib’s house arrest
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 11 — Fresh from resigning from the federal Cabinet, DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke has urged voters in Melaka who are aggrieved by former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest to channel their dissatisfaction through the ballot box in Saturday’s state election. Addressing a Pakatan Harapan ceramah in Ayer Keroh last night, Loke acknowledged widespread public indignation over the decision, while noting that the royal prerogative of mercy enshrined in the Federal Constitution must be respected. “I am sure many people cannot accept the fact that Najib can serve his sentence under house arrest.

items.title: CoreWeave targets 2028 profitability as AI demand surges
items.summary: CoreWeave had about US$46.9 billion in total debt as of the end of September. CoreWeave's revenue backlog stood at US$132.5 billion at September's end, rising from US$104 billion at the end of June. CoreWeave now expects 2026 revenue to be between US$13.0 billion and US$13.3 billion, from US$12.4 billion to US$13.2 billion earlier.

items.title: Semporna resort had no licence, no expat approval and seven Chinese ‘tourists’ on staff
items.summary: TAWAU, Nov 11 — Seven male tourists from China were arrested for allegedly misusing their Social Visit Passes to work at a tourist resort suspected operating illegally in Semporna. They were among 32 foreigners detained during a two-day Sabah Immigration Department operation in Tawau and Semporna, which began on Sunday. Sabah Immigration Department Director Datuk Sh Sitti Saleha Habib Yussof said her team inspected six premises and 324 individuals during the operation.

items.title: A glowing thing in the sky at 4.40am? Kunak is asking what it was
items.summary: KUNAK, Nov 11 — A glowing object was spotted moving across the district’s skies at 4.40am on Monday. The phenomenon was recorded by a fisherman who happened to be aboard a fishing boat at sea when the object was seen moving across the sky. The footage raised questions about the object’s identity and origin, including whether it could be linked to a particular atmospheric phenomenon.

items.title: Malaysia must bolster cyber resilience as Europe supermarket attacks expose risks - Experts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia needs to strengthen its operational cyber resilience, as recent attacks targeting supermarket refrigeration systems in Europe have exposed vulnerabilities in connected systems that could disrupt food supply chains, according to a cyber security expert. Adjunct Professor of Cybersecurity Practice at the University Malaysia of Computer Science and Engineering (UNIMY), Murugason R. Thangaratnam, said attackers did not need advanced hacking skills, as everyday connected systems, such as refrigeration controllers, building management systems and monitoring platforms, were built for convenience and uninterrupted operation rather than security. It is how operational technology (OT) security is converging with information technology (IT) security.

items.title: Microsoft presses Trump to scuttle ban on Chinese data centre tech
items.summary: Reuters reported in August that the Trump administration wants to ban US imports of new models of Chinese optical transceivers, which allow data to travel over fibre-optic cables at the speed of light within data centres. The concern is that they could be used by Beijing to steal data, install malware or disrupt service at US data centres. Microsoft has 35 data centres under construction in the US and another 134 planned, according to Cleanview, a market intelligence company which tracks data centre development.

items.title: Old EV batteries could power rural clinics and villages, Nga Kor Ming tells COP31
items.summary: Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said the proposal, known as the “Circular Equity Dividend”, was among three solutions put forward by Malaysia to accelerate urban circularity globally and advance the zero-waste agenda. “Malaysia’s Circular Economy Blueprint for Solid Waste 2025-2035 sets national targets of achieving a 40 per cent recycling rate and diverting 53 per cent of waste from landfills by 2035, supported by initiatives such as Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR), Separation at Source (SAS) and pilot Zero Waste Districts in Kuala Lumpur and Penang. “In 2024, Malaysia generated 14.5 million tonnes of municipal solid waste, with food waste accounting for 44.5 per cent and plastics 13.2 per cent, while more than RM2 billion is spent annually on waste management,” he said in a statement issued by the ministry.

items.title: 16 rescued from Nibong Tebal flash floods, car damaged by falling tree
items.summary: NIBONG TEBAL: Continuous heavy rain triggered flash floods overnight, trapping 16 residents from three families in Kampung Sethu, Sungai Bakap, early today. Penang Fire and Rescue Department operations division assistant director John Sagun Francis said firefighters were deployed to the scene following a distress call at 12.40am. " Rescuers found several houses submerged under about three feet 0.9m of flood water following persistent downpours.

items.title: Perak police seize 48 bitcoin mining machines in Seri Iskandar power theft raid
items.summary: IPOH, Nov 11 — A total of 48 units of cryptocurrency (bitcoin) mining machines were seized by the police in an operation yesterday at a residential premises in the Seri Iskandar area, which is believed to be the location for the mining activities with illegal electrical wire connections. Perak Tengah district police chief Supt Hafezul Helmi Hamzah said the raid was conducted by the Criminal Investigation Division of the Perak Tengah district police headquarters (IPD) in collaboration with the Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) engineering team. “In addition, two units of fast ethernet switches, one Internet router unit, and one cut electrical cable roll were also seized.

items.title: Australia home loans plunge 15.5pct in September quarter amid investor exodus
items.summary: Wednesday's data from the Australian Bureau of Statistics showed total new home loans fell 15.5 per cent by value in the September quarter to A$81.16 billion (US$55.6 billion), for a third straight quarter of declines. The number of loans dropped 15 per cent in the quarter. Loans for owner occupiers fell 5.3 per cent by value, while those for investment properties dropped a steep 32.3 per cent.

items.title: More boots on the ground: Kelantan Fire Dept weighs 24- or 48-hour duty shifts during monsoon season
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Nov 11 — The Kelantan Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) is considering extending the duty shifts of its personnel to up to 48 hours in the event of major flooding during the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon (MTL), to strengthen its rescue operation capabilities. In a related development, Kelantan JBPM has identified vulnerable groups, including the elderly, persons with disabilities (PwDs) and bedridden patients living in flood-prone areas, to facilitate evacuation efforts in the event of flooding. He said the exercise was carried out in coordination with the State Disaster Management Committee, involving the Social Welfare Department (JKM) and the Health Department.

items.title: Nvidia faces deepening scrutiny over China chip ties, CEO affair
items.summary: NEW YORK: Nvidia shed about US$430 billion in market value over two sessions as new reports deepened questions about CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a Chinese businesswoman alleged to be a spy for Beijing. The controversy escalated on several fronts on Tuesday as allegations emerged that Huang's relationship with Alice Huang aided at least US$7.5 billion in Nvidia chip shipments to China and that US Secretary of State Marco Rubio had previously briefed President Donald Trump on the affair. The FBI is separately examining whether 63-year-old Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation.

items.title: Kennedy family tries to stop Trump's Washington arch
items.summary: Several members of the Kennedy family, one of America's most famous political dynasties, filed on Tuesday to join a court case aimed at stopping President Donald Trump from building a proposed triumphal arch in Washington, saying it would obstruct views and cast shadows over their relatives' grave sites. The Kennedy family is one of the most prolific political dynasties in US history, notably including former President John F. Kennedy. Trump's health secretary is Robert F. Kennedy Jr., nephew to the assassinated former president.

items.title: Anthony Loke quits Cabinet but says DAP still has Anwar’s back
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 11 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim should not bow to political pressure to dissolve Parliament ahead of schedule. DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said the power and prerogative to advise the Yang di-Pertuan Agong on the dissolution of Parliament rested solely with the prime minister. “We know they are trying to capitalise on the current momentum to pressure the prime minister into dissolving Parliament.

items.title: Kelantan fire dept mulls 48-hour shifts for major flood operations
items.summary: KOTA BARU: The Kelantan Fire and Rescue Department is considering extending the duty shifts of its personnel to up to 48 hours in the event of major flooding during the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon (MTL), to strengthen its rescue operation capabilities. He said personnel currently work in three teams on a 12-hour shift system to ensure fire station operations continue around the clock. He said a freeze on leave could also be imposed, depending on the severity of the disaster, to ensure sufficient manpower, particularly when rescue operations require the deployment of more personnel.

items.title: In Dewan Rakyat today: Social media age verification, travel bans over tax, and solar schemes in focus
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — The enforcement status of social media age verification and restrictions on overseas travel were among the issues in focus at the Dewan Rakyat today. According to the Order Paper published on the Parliament’s official website, Wong Shu Qi (PH-Kluang) will ask the Communications Minister about the enforcement status of social media age verification since June 1, as well as action against platforms that had yet to implement the verification process and the status of the six-month transition period, during the question-and-answer session. Chow Yu Hui (PH-Raub) will ask the Finance Minister whether the Inland Revenue Board has the authority to restrict overseas travel over outstanding instalments under the CP500 tax instalment payment notice.

items.title: House Democrats to investigate Trump's handling of US spy agencies
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Democrats in the US House of Representatives, who will control key committees next year, are preparing investigations into what they say was President Donald Trump's politicisation and gutting of US spy agencies, including whether analysts have censored themselves to avoid retaliation. Former Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard last year cut her agency's staff by about 40%. The cuts included the firings of longtime intelligence analysts and officers from top posts, including at the National Intelligence Council, the analytical group overseen by the Office of the Director of National Intelligence.

items.title: Ringgit opens higher against major currencies, flat against greenback
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against major currencies but remained flat against the US dollar amid renewed expectations of a possible US Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hike following stronger-than-expected inflation data. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said US inflation data had heightened concerns over further monetary tightening, with the US Consumer Price Index (CPI) rising 0.4 per cent month-on-month in October, above the consensus estimate of 0.3 per cent. He said the prospect of higher interest rates also pushed yield on the two-year US Treasury note up by 18 basis points to 4.74 per cent, while the US Dollar Index strengthened 0.57 per cent to 102.233 points.

items.title: US dollar ticks up
items.summary: NEW YORK: The United States (US) dollar increased in late trading on Tuesday, reported Xinhua. In late New York trading, the euro was down to US$1.1166 from US$1.1223 in the previous session, and the British pound declined to US$1.3348 from US$1.3439 in the last session. The US dollar bought 158.78 Japanese yen, higher than 157.77 Japanese yen of the previous session.

items.title: Social media age verification, travel restrictions among focus of today's Dewan Rakyat sitting
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The enforcement status of social media age verification and restrictions on overseas travel were among the issues in focus at the Dewan Rakyat today. According to the Order Paper published on the Parliament's official website, Wong Shu Qi (PH-Kluang) will ask the communications minister about the enforcement status of social media age verification since June 1, as well as action against platforms that had yet to implement the verification process and the status of the six-month transition period, during the question-and-answer session. Chow Yu Hui (PH-Raub) will ask the finance minister whether the Inland Revenue Board has the authority to restrict overseas travel over outstanding instalments under the CP500 tax instalment payment notice.

items.title: Crude Futures Settle Lower
items.summary: NEW YORK: Oil prices fell on Tuesday, reported Xinhua. The West Texas Intermediate for December delivery decreased by US$0.81, or 0.93 per cent, to settle at US$86.04 a barrel on the New York Mercantile Exchange. Brent crude for January delivery dropped to US$1.08, or 1.17 per cent, to settle at US$91.49 a barrel on the London ICE Futures Exchange.

items.title: Tighter scrutiny expected on Malaysia as Nvidia scandal spills over
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia could face tighter scrutiny by the United States over advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chip shipments following allegations that Nvidia graphic processing units (GPUs) were diverted to China, although a blanket ban on supplies is unlikely for now. "The bigger concern is whether Malaysia's reputation as a trusted semiconductor and technology hub could be affected, potentially making access to advanced AI chips more costly and time-consuming," BIMB Securities chief economist Imran Nurginias told Business Times. Following the latest news, the US Congress is more likely to pass legislation aimed at tightening China's access to AI chips.

items.title: UK arrests US army member suspected of spying for Russia
items.summary: LONDON: A member of the US military was arrested in Britain on Tuesday on suspicion of spying for Russia, London police said. "The 41-year-old man was arrested near Gloucester on Tuesday," London Metropolitan police said in a statement, adding that "The country to which the allegations relate is Russia." The suspect was a member of the US Army and was being held at a London jail, police said, adding that they worked closely with US authorities on the case.

items.title: Thomas Markle ordered back to jail after cutting off his ankle bracelet
items.summary: LOS ANGELES: Thomas Markle, an accused child sexual predator and the estranged father of Britain's Duchess of Sussex Meghan Markle, was ordered back to jail on Tuesday after cutting of an electronic monitoring device he was supposed to wear as a condition of home confinement, federal prosecutors said. US Magistrate Judge Lindsay Saxe Griffin ordered the 82-year-old father-in-law of Prince Harry returned to federal detention without bond at a hearing in Tampa, Florida, according to the US Attorney's Office in Los Angeles, where the case against him is pending. According to an FBI affidavit filed in court as part of the criminal complaint lodged against Markle, federal agents seized the material in question, part of a cache of slides, film negatives and books, from storage units Markle had rented in Los Angeles since 2008.

items.title: ECRL, bus, plane or car? Weighing the cost, time and convenience of getting to the East Coast
items.summary: But choosing how to travel may depend on more than just the ticket price, as the ECRL, buses, flights and driving each come with different trade-offs in journey time, convenience and overall door-to-door costs. However, fares may vary depending on travel time, demand and seat availability. However, the journey takes about nine hours and 30 minutes under ideal traffic conditions.

items.title: How much has China influenced Chinese Malaysian youths?
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — China’s growing influence among Chinese Malaysians youths is increasingly visible not only through the products they buy, but also through the entertainment, social media platforms and language trends. Participants in a recently published IMAN Research study described exposure to Chinese digital platforms and content, including trends, slang and expressions, have spread beyond China through online communities. However, the researchers found that consuming Chinese content did not automatically change how participants viewed their national identity.

items.title: IMAN Research finds gaps in how Chinese youths understand politics and public institutions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — A young Chinese individual may know about the latest political controversy, follow debates on social media or have strong views about the rising cost of living. That gap between following politics and understanding how the system works emerged as one of the findings in a recently published IMAN Research study on Malaysian Chinese youths. Who shapes their political understanding?

items.title: US lawmakers urge new Epstein investigations in damning report
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US lawmakers called for further criminal investigations into associates of notorious sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, in a scathing report blaming prosecutors, financial institutions and powerful connections for allowing his abuse to continue for years. The Epstein saga has dogged President Donald Trump, who was friends with the financier for years but has denied any knowledge of his crimes. The report also called for further questioning of another longtime Epstein assistant, Lesley Groff, over her possible knowledge of his crimes.

items.title: Content Forum moots regional safeguards
items.summary: SOUTHEAST Asian countries should adopt common minimum safeguards to protect children from commercial risks in the digital economy. Content Forum put forward the proposals at the Asean ICT Forum on Child Online Protection in Manila last week. Mediha said children's growing involvement in the digital economy had exposed them to commercial risks that were often overlooked.

items.title: Penang welcomes inaugural winter charter flight from Poland
items.summary: PENANG has welcomed its first winter charter flight from Warsaw, marking a new addition to Malaysia's international air travel. The passengers were welcomed in a ceremony jointly organised by Penang Global Tourism (PGT) and Tourism Malaysia, together with tourism stakeholders and industry partners. Tourism Malaysia said the service reflected growing interest among Polish travellers in Malaysia's cultural heritage, tropical islands, nature-based attractions and gastronomy.

items.title: Trump ally elected US House Republican leader after election rout
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Jim Jordan, a hardline ally of President Donald Trump, was elected leader of the Republicans in the US House of Representatives on Tuesday, defeating fellow conservative Steve Scalise as the party reckons with a crushing midterm election defeat. Jordan, the combative chairman of the House Judiciary Committee, beat the current majority leader by 106 votes to 73 in a secret ballot, US media reported, putting him in charge of the party's opposition to the incoming Democratic majority. Senate Republicans meanwhile reelected John Thune as their leader, retaining their existing leadership team despite demands from conservatives for a reckoning over the election losses.

items.title: Boeing to cut 5pc of commercial jet workforce
items.summary: SEATTLE: Boeing Commercial Airplanes plans to cut five per cent of its workforce as it struggles to increase jetliner production, division chief Stephanie Pope told employees recently in an internal memo. "Adjusting our production schedules and reducing aircraft output puts us in an overstaffed position," Pope said in the memo reviewed by Reuters. Boeing chief executive officer Kelly Ortberg told analysts last month the company would miss its 737 jetliner production and delivery targets this year.

items.title: Nvidia heads for US$470 billion two-day wipeout as CEO affair fallout deepens
items.summary: The CEO's relationship with Alice Huang helped facilitate shipments of at least US$7.5 billion worth of Nvidia chips to Chinese firms, The Information reported on Tuesday, citing two people who know her. Alice Huang and Jensen Huang are not related. Trump said Huang told him he had "absolutely no idea" and that he believed the Nvidia CEO.

items.title: Loke challenges BN MPs to quit cabinet over criticism of Anwar
items.summary: MELAKA: DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke has challenged Barisan Nasional members of Parliament to resign from the cabinet instead of continuing to criticise the prime minister and the unity government while remaining in power. In his first public appearance after stepping down as transport minister, Loke said those who disagreed with Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's leadership should uphold the principle of collective responsibility by relinquishing their cabinet positions. If you disagree with the prime minister, resign.

items.title: Najib arrives at Taman Duta residence to begin his house arrest (VIDEO)
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak has arrived at his residence in Jalan Langgak Duta here today to begin serving the remainder of his SRC International prison sentence under house arrest. Najib’s arrival at his Taman Duta home followed a fresh High Court order this afternoon, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence at the residence until August 23, 2028. Aslam said the new order cancelled the November 6 order and replaced it with one allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his sentence at home.

items.title: ‘I should have stepped down today’: Hannah Yeoh says Anthony Loke paid the price instead
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said she should have resigned from the Cabinet today, but DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke wanted the party’s ministers to remain in government to fulfil their promises to the people. Her remarks came after Loke announced his resignation as transport minister with immediate effect, following the Kuala Lumpur High Court’s decision allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his SRC International prison sentence under house arrest. Loke had first announced his intention to resign in September following the conditional pardon granted to Najib, but remained in the Cabinet temporarily at Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s request.

items.title: Viral video leads to probe into firecracker incident in Klang
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 10 — Police are investigating an incident involving an individual setting off firecrackers at the traffic light junction of Jalan Tengku Kelana, Kawasan 1, Klang, which endangered public safety on Nov 8. South Klang district police chief ACP Lim Jit Huey said the incident, which occurred at about 1 am, went viral on social media before police received a report regarding the matter. “Those with information are urged to contact the South Klang District Police Headquarters or any nearby police station to assist in the investigation,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: ‘Alhamdulillah’: Rosmah welcomes news of Najib’s clearance for house arrest
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor has expressed gratitude following the return of her husband, former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, to their residence in Jalan Langgak Duta here today after a court order allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house detention. She said she was awaiting Najib’s arrival at their Taman Duta home, where he will serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house detention. Earlier today, the High Court issued a fresh order allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his reduced six-year prison term under house detention until Aug 23, 2028, with immediate effect.

items.title: Investigation papers on Penang assemblyman accused of injuring wife still under DPP review
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 10 — Penang police are awaiting further instructions from the Deputy Public Prosecutor (DPP) on the investigation into an allegation that a state assemblyman injured his wife in an incident on October 31. Penang Chief Police Officer Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said the investigation papers were still with the DPP's office for further review. "The investigation papers are still with the DPP, and police are awaiting further instructions on the case," he told Bernama when contacted tonight for an update on the investigation.

items.title: Home Ministry says ready to carry out Najib’s house arrest; court order today cleared the air
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — The Home Ministry this evening said it is prepared to carry out a new court order today for former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to be on house arrest until August 2028. In his statement on his ministry’s readiness to execute the court’s new order, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the High Court’s latest order has helped answered legal uncertainties surrounding Najib’s house arrest. He was referring to the High Court in Kuala Lumpur’s decision this afternoon to revoke an earlier November 6 “Order of Discharge on Payment of Fine” and to replace it with a new order that will require Najib to serve his remaining jail term under house arrest until August 23, 2028.

items.title: Najib’s house arrest: What did the AGC ask the High Court to clarify today?
items.summary: In its written application, the prosecution requested that the High Court replace a November 6 discharge order with new terms clarifying Najib’s remaining SRC International sentence and his subsequent imprisonment in the 1MDB case. It also sought to specify that his SRC sentence would end on August 23, 2028, with his return to prison subject to any court order then in force. High Court issues replacement order High Court judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin subsequently set aside the November 6 discharge order and issued a replacement order allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his SRC sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028.

items.title: How uncertainty over university pathways shapes Chinese youths’ choices
items.summary: In a research conducted by IMAN Research, they found that uncertainty over public university admissions, differences between pre-university pathways and concerns about access to certain courses had influenced how some the research participants approached their education. Some participants described choosing private education or overseas study rather than applying through the public university admission system. The report describes these decisions as examples of how young people may seek alternatives when public pathways appear uncertain.

items.title: Rapid KL confirms brake fault behind smoke incident at KL Sentral (VIDEO)
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — Rapid KL today confirmed an incident involving one of its trains at KL Sentral station after smoke was seen coming from the train at about 5.15pm. In a statement, the rail operator said the incident is believed to have been caused by the train's braking system, which resulted in visible smoke being emitted from the affected train. Rapid KL said all passengers were safely disembarked at Bangsar station and were able to continue their journey on the next available train.

items.title: Beyond assumptions: IMAN Research’s journey into the lives of Chinese youths
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — When Violet Lee Zi Yi began researching Malaysian Chinese youths, she admitted she initially approached the community with assumptions about its relative economic advantages, resources and access to opportunities. “I initially thought Chinese is a unitary block. It is so different,” Lee said in an interview about the findings of IMAN Research’s report, Kami Orang Sini Juga: Chinese Youths and Democratic Belonging — The Politics of Pragmatism and Fairness .

items.title: Anthony Loke officially resigns as transport minister following court decision on Najib
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke Siew Fook has resigned as transport minister with immediate effect following the Kuala Lumpur High Court's decision allowing former prime minister Najib Tun Razak to serve his sentence under house arrest, according to a statement issued today. He expressed his appreciation to Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim for the trust and mandate given to him to serve in the Cabinet since December 2022. Loke also thanked the senior management and staff of the Ministry of Transport for their commitment and cooperation throughout his tenure at the ministry.

items.title: Najib to serve remaining jail term at home after High Court issues new warrant
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — The High Court has directed the Court Registrar to issue a new order that would finally allow Datuk Seri Mohd Najib Abdul Razak to serve the remaining sentence of his first corruption conviction at home. High Court Judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin issued the new warrant of release after hearing submissions by both Najib’s lawyers and the Deputy Public Prosecutors this afternoon. Judge Aslam said the new order simply cancels the November 6 order and replaced with one that allows Najib to serve the remaining sentence from the said conviction at home.

items.title: Kuala Kangsar Sessions Court orders mental health assessment for accused in rape, attempted murder case
items.summary: KUALA KANGSAR, Nov 10 — The Sessions Court here today ordered a man who pleaded guilty to attempting to murder and raping a woman to undergo a psychiatric assessment at Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta, Tanjung Rambutan. Judge Nuur Hafiedzah Md Daud issued the order against Marwan Mohd Nor, 38, under Section 342 of the Criminal Procedure Code after observing the accused’s demeanour when he pleaded guilty to both charges. Earlier, Marwan pleaded guilty to both charges and appealed to the court to impose the maximum sentence for the rape charge.

items.title: ITU PP-26: Appointment of Malaysian representative as Committee 5 chair reflects international confidence
items.summary: DOHA, Nov 10 — Malaysia’s appointment as chair of Committee 5 at the 2026 International Telecommunication Union Plenipotentiary Conference (ITU PP-26) reflects the international community’s confidence in the country’s ability to play a neutral role in balancing the interests of various parties. Committee 5 chair Eneng Faridah Iskandar said the appointment was not merely a personal recognition but a major achievement for Malaysia, according to a report published by Bernama. Explaining Committee 5’s role, Eneng Faridah said the substantive committee was responsible for examining various policy and legal issues within the ITU framework.

items.title: Not cutting-edge: Men armed with scissors in Tuaran gang robbery to be sentenced on Nov 20
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Nov 10 — Three men who pleaded guilty to a charge of gang robbery armed with scissors will know their fate on November 20. Sessions Court Judge Monica Linsua adjourned the sentencing of the men, aged 29, 26, and 35 respectively, under Section 395 of the Penal Code, which is punishable under Section 397 of the same Code, at the request of the prosecution. The men had admitted robbing another two men of their cash and two mobile phones by the roadside of Jalan Berungis in Tuaran at 12.50am on Oct 26.

items.title: MWC Doha: Fahmi shares Malaysia’s 5G network progress, 90pc coverage achieved ahead of schedule
items.summary: DOHA, Nov 10 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil shared Malaysia’s progress in expanding its 5G network at Mobile World Congress (MWC) Doha 2026, with the country’s second 5G network achieving 90 per cent coverage last October, nine months ahead of schedule. Fahmi said Malaysia had also made substantial investments in expanding and strengthening its digital infrastructure through the National Digital Network Plan (Jendela) since 2020. However, Fahmi stressed that Malaysia’s digital infrastructure development was not solely focused on expanding network coverage, but also on service quality, subscription affordability and network resilience.

items.title: Najib in court as lawyers, AGC discuss fresh house arrest order
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — Datuk Seri Najib Razak is present as the High Court hears the application for a new order to allow the former prime minister to serve his first jail sentence at home. Najib, in a light blue baju melayu top with sleeves rolled up, was present at the hearing alongside his daughter Najwa, who was in a blue floral baju kurung. The High Court is expected to issue a new warrant to release Najib from Kajang Prison this afternoon itself.

items.title: Melaka polls: Pakatan takes politics to coffee shops with Gen Z-focused ‘Kopilih Harapan’ initiative
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 10 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is adopting a new approach to engage young people, particularly Generation Z, through its ‘Kopilih Harapan’ programme, which provides an informal platform for political leaders and members of the public to discuss current issues and aspirations. PH Election Department (JPPH) Media Unit head Jonathan Vela said the programme aims to foster more open and inclusive two-way communication, moving away from conventional political ceramah. He said the coffee shop-themed initiative allows young people to raise questions, share their views and seek clarification directly from PH leaders and candidates.

items.title: Skilled workforce crucial to unlocking Malaysia’s high-tech investment potential, says minister
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Nov 10 — Developing a highly skilled workforce must remain a priority for Malaysia to fully capitalise on opportunities arising from digital transformation and the rapid growth of high-tech industries. Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Datuk Chang Lih Kang said that while Malaysia continues to attract billions of ringgit in high-tech sector investments, the country’s success ultimately depends on its local workforce’s ability to master and harness emerging technologies. Chang said industry investments in human capital development also reinforced the principle that Malaysia’s greatest asset was its people, ensuring national innovation policies translated into tangible economic outcomes.
